claim: Saccharomyces cerevisiae lacks homologs to genes that make up the core oscillator or light-sensing pathways of fungal circadian rhythms.
source: The budding yeast, Saccharomyces cerevisiae, lacks homologs to genes that make up the core oscillator or light-sensing pathways of fungal circadian rhythms (Brunner and Kaldi, 2008; Idnurm and Heitman, 2010; Salichos and Rokas, 2010)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to three published studies that have investigated the presence of circadian clock genes in S. cerevisiae.

claim: Saccharomyces cerevisiae does not display any 24-hr behavior capable of sustained autonomous oscillations in a constant environment.
source: and does not display any 24-hr behavior capable of sustained autonomous oscillations in a constant environment (Eelderink-Chen et al., 2010; Robertson et al., 2013)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to two published studies that examined oscillatory behavior in S. cerevisiae.

claim: Yellow fluorescent protein (YFP) was expressed from the promoter of the FLO1 gene in the experimental strain.
source: We expressed yellow fluorescent protein (YFP) from the promoter of the FLO1 gene (Verstrepen et al., 2005; Rando and Verstrepen, 2007; Verstrepen and Fink, 2009)
evidence: This is a direct statement about the experimental design with citations to relevant literature about the FLO1 gene.

claim: The mutation rate was elevated about 100-fold by mutating the proof-reading activity of DNA polymerase δ (POL3).
source: and elevated the mutation rate about 100-fold by mutating the proof-reading activity of DNA polymerase ∂ (POL3) (Jin et al., 2005)
evidence: This claim describes a specific experimental manipulation with a citation to the method.

claim: Two parallel populations were evolved using selection strengths of the top and bottom 6% (E6) or 15% (E15) of events detected by FACS.
source: We evolved two parallel populations using two different strengths of selection: the top and bottom 6% (E6) or 15% (E15) of the events detected by FACS.
evidence: This is a direct description of the experimental design.

claim: Selected cells proliferated for roughly six divisions before the next selection.
source: The selected cells proliferated for roughly six divisions before the next selection.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the experimental protocol.

claim: The selection scheme selects for synchrony rather than entrainment.
source: Our scheme selects for synchrony rather than entrainment: twice a day, we select the cells with high or low fluorescence, rather than varying an environmental cue and selecting for a response to it.
evidence: This is an explicit interpretation of the experimental design by the authors.

claim: After 30 days of selection, the intensity distributions resulting from the selections for high and low fluorescence differed.
source: After 30 days of selection, the intensity distributions resulting from the selections for high and low fluorescence differed.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an experimental observation.

claim: Both evolved populations showed a cyclical change in the fluorescence distribution after synchronization, with the E6 population giving larger shifts than the less strongly selected E15.
source: After synchronization, both evolved populations showed a cyclical change in the fluorescence distribution, with the E6 population giving larger shifts than the less strongly selected E15 (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by both the text description and reference to Figure 1C showing the data.

claim: The distribution of RFP also cycled in the evolved populations.
source: To our surprise, the distribution of RFP also cycled (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This claim is supported by the text statement and reference to figure data.

claim: Just before selection for low fluorescence, the population was predominantly single-celled, and just before selection for high fluorescence, most cells were in multicellular clumps.
source: Just before their scheduled selection for low fluorescence, the population was predominantly single-celled, and just before their selection for high fluorescence, most cells were in multicellular clumps (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by both text description and microscopy images in Figure 1D.

claim: The fluorescence per cell is constant over 24 hr for both YFP and RFP.
source: The fluorescence per cell is constant over 24 hr, for both YFP and RFP, and thus the cyclical variation in intensity seen by FACS is entirely due to changes in cell association (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by text and reference to figure data showing fluorescence measurements.

claim: The cyclical variation in intensity seen by FACS is entirely due to changes in cell association.
source: The fluorescence per cell is constant over 24 hr, for both YFP and RFP, and thus the cyclical variation in intensity seen by FACS is entirely due to changes in cell association (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that per-cell fluorescence is constant while total fluorescence varies.

claim: All 30 isolated clones (15 from each population) produced strong oscillations in YFP and RFP distributions.
source: We isolated and analyzed fifteen clones from each population after subjecting them to FACS-based synchronization: all 30 clones produced strong oscillations in YFP and RFP distributions
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental results from testing multiple clones.

claim: The cycle is not a response to daily variations in environmental factors such as temperature.
source: The cycle is not a response to daily variations in environmental factors such as temperature.
evidence: This claim is supported by the control experiment described in the following text and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: A population subjected to identical manipulations without fluorescence-based selection did not oscillate, while a FACS-synchronized population did oscillate.
source: The first population oscillated, showing primarily single cells just before the selection for low YFP fluorescence, and primarily clumps just before the selection for high YFP fluorescence, whereas the unsynchronized population showed very similar distributions at these two times (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C, D).
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental comparison described in text and shown in the figure.

claim: Single cells emerging from the single-cell phase build lineage-based clumps.
source: The absence of clumps containing more than one yellow cell or both CFP+ and CFP− cells in the same clump shows that cells emerging from the single-cell phase build lineage-based clumps.
evidence: This is an inference based on the cell labeling experiment showing clumps contain only one labeled founder cell and cells of one CFP genotype.

claim: Synchronous oscillations in cell association were observed even at very high dilution (~10³ cells/ml).
source: Consistent with this interpretation, we saw synchronous oscillations in cell association even at very high dilution (∼103 cells/ml).
evidence: This is a direct statement of an experimental observation.

claim: Multicellular clumps give rise to single cells by fragmenting to produce smaller clumps and proliferating to produce single-celled offspring.
source: Multicellular clumps, which were covalently labeled at the time of peak aggregation gave rise to single cells by a combination of two mechanisms: fragmenting to produce smaller clumps and proliferating to produce single-celled offspring.
evidence: This claim is based on observations from the cell wall labeling experiments described in the text and shown in Figure 2.

claim: Clumps form by cells sticking together rather than failing to separate after division.
source: When unsynchronized CFP+ and CFP− subclones were sonicated to break up all the clumps and cultured together for 90 min, clumps that re-associated were composed of a mixture of CFP+ and CFP− cells showing that clumps form by cells sticking together rather than failing to separate after division (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by the mixing experiment showing that clumps can contain cells of different genotypes.

claim: Cells oscillate between two states over a 24-hr period: single cells produce offspring that stick to their mothers to assemble lineage-based clumps, which later produce single cells and small clumps.
source: These results show that cells oscillate between two states over a 24-hr period: single cells produce offspring that immediately stick to their mothers to assemble a lineage-based clump, which later produces a population of single cells and small clumps as a result of clumps fragmenting and producing single cells which divide to produce a mixture of small clumps and single cells (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a summary claim based on multiple experimental observations described in the text and figures.

claim: Free run populations continued to show detectable oscillations after synchronization was stopped.
source: The free run populations continued to show detectable oscillations, which were undetectable in a control population that had not been synchronized (Unsynch) (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by the free run experiment data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Individual cell lineages produced sustained oscillations for 3 days without FACS-based synchronization.
source: Cell lineages produced sustained oscillations for 3 days (Figure 3C) with many lineages remaining in phase with each other.
evidence: This claim is supported by the single lineage tracking experiment shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Some lineages shifted their phase within a 24-hr period, but the overall period over 3 cycles was approximately 24 hr.
source: In some lineages, their phase shifted within a 24-hr period, but the overall period, over 3 cycles was approximately 24 hr.
evidence: This is an observation from the lineage tracking experiment.

claim: The evolved populations have an autonomous oscillator capable of sustained oscillations in the absence of an environmental stimulus.
source: These results suggest that we have evolved an autonomous oscillator capable of sustained oscillations in the absence of an environmental stimulus.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the free run experiments showing continued oscillations without selection or environmental cues.

claim: Eight mutations were classified as putative causal mutations based on being present in ≥95% of selected cells in bulk segregant analysis.
source: We classified eight mutations that were present in ≥95% of the selected cells as putative causal mutations (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is based on the bulk segregant analysis method and the threshold used for identifying causal mutations.

claim: Engineering the eight putative causal mutations into a wild type laboratory strain recreated the evolved oscillator.
source: We recreated the evolved oscillator by engineering these eight mutations into a wild type laboratory strain.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental approach and result.

claim: The oscillations of the recreated strain are indistinguishable from those of E6-1 after synchronization.
source: After synchronization, the oscillations of the recreated strain are indistinguishable from those of E6-1 (Figure 4B)
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The recreated strain shows similar free run behavior as E6-1 both as populations and as single lineages.
source: and produce a similar free run behavior as E6-1 both as populations (Figure 4C) and as single lineages (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by the free run experiments shown in Figures 4C and 4D.

claim: Each causative mutation could be individually replaced by a gene deletion without destroying the oscillation.
source: Each causative mutation could be individually replaced by a gene deletion without destroying the oscillation (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is based on systematic gene deletion experiments shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Only two genes (SIR4 and YJL070C) substantially altered the oscillations when replaced with wild-type versions: SIR4 made E6-1 single-celled and YJL070C produced constitutive clumps.
source: Surprisingly, only two genes substantially altered the oscillations: SIR4 made E6-1 single-celled and YJL070C produced constitutive clumps (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is based on the wild-type replacement experiments shown in Figure 5B.

claim: sir4-100 was selected for in all conditions in the sub-trait selection experiments.
source: In three independent replicate experiments, sir4-100 was selected for in all conditions
evidence: This claim is based on the sub-trait selection experiments described in the text and shown in Figure 5C.

claim: scw11-E261* was selected for in constitutive clumps.
source: scw11-E261* was selected for in constitutive clumps
evidence: This claim is based on the sub-trait selection experiments.

claim: Three mutations (vps5-S520L, pet127-D650N, and whi2-R127*) were positively selected for in single cells and selected against in clumping cells.
source: and three mutations, vps5-S520L, pet127-D650N, and whi2-R127* were positively selected for in single cells and selected against in clumping cells.
evidence: This claim is based on the sub-trait selection experiments shown in Figure 5C.

claim: There were 155 genes whose expression differed between the ancestral and evolved populations.
source: There were 155 genes whose expression differed between the ancestral and evolved populations (Figure 5D and Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is based on RNA-seq data comparing gene expression between strains.

claim: Haploid-specific genes were repressed in the evolved clone E6-1.
source: Haploid-specific genes (hsg), which are normally expressed in haploids and repressed in diploids, were repressed in the evolved clone
evidence: This claim is based on gene expression analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: 8 of the 10 most strongly repressed genes in E6-1 were haploid-specific.
source: 8 of the 10 most strongly repressed genes were haploid-specific.
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the gene expression data.

claim: The repression of haploid-specific genes in E6-1 is due to the causal mutation that inactivates SIR4.
source: This phenotype is due to the causal mutation that inactivates SIR4, a gene required for transcriptional silencing of sub-telomeric genes, and the mating genes at the two silenced loci, HMLα and HMRa (Rine and Herskowitz, 1987; Herskowitz, 1988; Pillus and Rine, 1989).
evidence: This claim is based on known functions of SIR4 from the literature and the observation that sir4 mutation is present in E6-1.

claim: In sir4 cells, the expression of a and α information from HMLα and HMRa mimics a diploid cell and represses haploid-specific genes.
source: In sir4 cells, the expression of a and α information from these two loci mimics a diploid cell and represses haploid-specific genes.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about mating type regulation in yeast.

claim: Deleting HMLα from the evolved clone E6-1 restores the haploid pattern of gene expression and eliminates cell clumping.
source: Consistent with the effect of expressing SIR4 in E6-1, deleting HMLα from the evolved clone, which removes the only source of α information restores the haploid pattern of gene expression and eliminates cell clumping (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental results shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: None of the causative mutations in E6-1 reached a frequency above 0.4 in the overall E6 population by the end of evolution.
source: None of the mutations in E6-1 reached a frequency above 0.4
evidence: This claim is based on Sanger sequencing of the E6 population at different time points, shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Two of the causative mutations in E6-1 were undetectable in the overall E6 population.
source: two were undetectable in the overall population
evidence: This is based on the time course sequencing data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Six causative mutations in E6-1 were first detected between 12 and 30 days of evolution.
source: and the remaining six were first detected between 12 and 30 days of evolution (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is based on the time course data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: All clones from the evolved populations cycled, suggesting the populations have multiple lineages.
source: All the clones from the evolved populations cycled suggesting that the populations have multiple lineages.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that all tested clones showed cycling behavior.

claim: E6-2 contained 6 of the 8 causative mutations found in E6-1 and had three additional putative causative mutations.
source: E6-2 contained 6 of the 8 causative mutations found in E6-1 and had three additional putative causative mutations.
evidence: This claim is based on bulk segregant analysis and sequencing of clone E6-2, shown in Figure 6B.

claim: E6-3 and E6-4 share three mutations but have no mutations in common with the lineage that produced E6-1 and E6-2.
source: E6-3 and E6-4 share three mutations, but have no mutations in common with the lineage that produced E6-1 and E6-2.
evidence: This claim is based on bulk segregant analysis of multiple clones shown in Figure 6B.

claim: There are at least five independently evolved oscillators in the E6 and E15 populations based on WHI2 allele analysis.
source: Analyzing the entire open reading frame of WHI2, the one gene that was mutated in all 4 sequenced clones, suggests that there are at least five independently evolved oscillators in the E6 and E15 populations, since one population (E6) contains 2 mutant and one wild-type allele, and the other contains one mutant and one wild-type allele (Figure 6—source data 1B).
evidence: This is an inference based on the diversity of WHI2 alleles found across different clones.

claim: All nine tested clones have increased expression of HMLα and reduced expression of haploid-specific genes compared to the ancestor.
source: All nine clones have increased expression of HMLα and reduced expression of haploid-specific genes when compared to the ancestor (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is based on qPCR measurements shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Deleting HMLα resulted in a loss of multicellular aggregates in all but one clone (E6-5).
source: Furthermore, deleting HMLα in these clones resulted in a loss of multicellular aggregates in all but one clone (Figure 6D, E6-5)
evidence: This claim is based on the experimental results shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Only one of the clones (E6-2) has the sir4 allele found in E6-1.
source: even though only one of the clones (E6-2) has the sir4 allele found in E6-1.
evidence: This is based on the sequencing data from multiple clones shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The 24-hr cycles that can be driven by temperature oscillations rapidly die out at constant temperature.
source: Fluctuations in metabolic activity can be driven by temperature oscillations with a 24-hr period but rapidly die out at constant temperature (Eelderink-Chen et al., 2010)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a published study.

claim: A particular regime of growth to high density can induce prolonged metabolic oscillations with a period of 4–5 hr.
source: and a particular regime of growth to high density can induce prolonged metabolic oscillations whose period is 4–5 hr (Tu et al., 2005)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a published study.

claim: The evolved yeast oscillator has a roughly 24-hr period that is maintained in the absence of environmental cues or selection on the output of the oscillator.
source: Our results show the yeast oscillator we evolved has two of these four behaviors: its roughly 24-hr period is maintained in the absence of environmental cues or selection on the output of the oscillator (Figures 2B, 3A, 3C, 4C, and 4D)
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple figures showing free run experiments.

claim: The evolved yeast oscillator regulates a cellular behavior: the ability of cells to form clumps.
source: and it regulates a cellular behavior, the ability of cells to form clumps.
evidence: This is a summary of the observed phenotype throughout the paper.

claim: Multiple combinations of mutations can produce the same complex phenotype.
source: The ability of multiple combinations of mutations to produce the same complex phenotype leads to two inferences.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that different clones with different mutations all show oscillatory behavior.

claim: The few mutations that are shared between different oscillating lineages suggest that there are multiple, functionally different ways that rearrangements can lead to the same phenotype.
source: The few mutations that are shared between different oscillating lineages suggest that there are multiple, functionally different ways that such rearrangements can lead to the same phenotype.
evidence: This is an inference based on the genetic diversity observed among different oscillating clones.

claim: All nine examined populations have switched from the haploid- to the diploid-specific pattern of gene expression.
source: All nine of the populations we examined have switched from the haploid- to the diploid-specific pattern of gene expression
evidence: This claim is based on gene expression analysis of multiple clones shown in Figure 6C.

claim: All four lineages analyzed in detail have mutated WHI2.
source: and all four lineages analyzed in detail have mutated WHI2.
evidence: This claim is based on sequencing data from four clones shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Four of the six mutations that are strongly identified as causal mutations are loss of function mutations.
source: Four of the six mutations that are strongly identified as causal mutations are loss of function mutations.
evidence: This is an inference based on the nature of the mutations (nonsense mutations and deletions that phenocopy the evolved alleles).

claim: The mutations in SCW11 and WHI2 are nonsense mutations.
source: The mutations in SCW11 and WHI2 are nonsense mutations
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Mutations in SIR4 and YJL070C can be replaced by gene deletions but not by restoration of the wild-type gene.
source: whereas those in SIR4 and YJL070C can be replaced by gene deletions, but not by restoration of the wild-type gene.
evidence: This claim is based on the deletion and wild-type replacement experiments shown in Figures 5A and 5B.

claim: The preponderance of loss of function mutants suggests that sophisticated functions can be produced primarily by inactivating genes, rather than modifying or increasing their activities.
source: The preponderance of loss of function mutants suggests that sophisticated functions can be produced primarily by inactivating genes, rather than modifying or increasing their activities.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that most causal mutations are loss-of-function.

claim: The W303 S. cerevisiae strain background was used for all experiments.
source: The W303 S. cerevisiae strain background was used for all experiments.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the experimental materials.

claim: Standard rich media (YPD) was used for all experiments: 2% Peptone, 2% D-Glucose, and 1% Yeast-Extract supplemented with Penicillin/Streptomycin.
source: Standard rich media (YPD) was used for all experiments: 2% Peptone, 2% D-Glucose, and 1% Yeast-Extract supplemented with Penicillin/Streptomycin (Sigma P0781).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the experimental conditions.

claim: Analysis and sorting was performed on a MoFlo Legacy (Dako Cytomation/Beckman Coulter) with two excitation lasers.
source: Analysis and sorting was performed on a MoFlo Legacy (Dako Cytomation/Beckman Coulter) with two excitation lasers and respective filter settings: 488 nm-550/30, and 594 nm-630/40.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the experimental equipment and methods.

claim: The selection cycle was repeated for 30 continuous days during experimental evolution.
source: This cycle was repeated for 30 continuous days.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the duration of the experimental evolution.

claim: Cell densities were occasionally measured before FACS selection to ensure the population stayed below 1 × 10⁶ cells/ml.
source: Cell densities were occasionally measured before FACS selection to ensure the population stayed below 1 × 106 cells/ml.
evidence: This is a direct statement about quality control during the experimental evolution.
